topic: Automated Red Teaming for AI Agent Safety: A Practical Guide (2026)

competitors.title: DeepTeam — The LLM Red Teaming Framework
key_points: 50+ ready-to-use vulnerability types across 7 categories (Data Privacy, Responsible AI, Security, Safety, Business, Agentic, Custom)
20+ research-backed adversarial attack methods for single-turn and multi-turn red teaming
Built-in support for OWASP Top 10 for LLMs 2025, OWASP Top 10 for Agents 2026, NIST AI RMF, MITRE ATLAS
7 production-ready guardrails for real-time LLM input/output protection
CLI with YAML configs and Python programmatic API
2,180+ GitHub stars, open-source, runs locally

competitors.title: G0 — The Control Layer for AI Agents
key_points: 1,200+ risk patterns across 12 domains for AI agent estate scanning
4,000+ adversarial payloads for red teaming
Endpoint assessment: detects 19 AI developer tools and MCP server configurations
Fleet control plane for multi-repo/multi-machine agent estate management
MCP supply chain security: per-skill trust scoring, rug-pull detection
AI-BOM (Bill of Materials) generation with CycloneDX format
OWASP Agentic Top 10 aligned

competitors.title: Nyx — Multi-Turn Adaptive Offensive Testing Harness for AI Agents
key_points: Pure blackbox testing — no special access needed, tests like users interact
Multi-turn adaptive conversations that probe for logic bugs and reasoning failures
Multi-modal testing: voice, text, images, documents, browser interactions
Massively parallel by default
Finds issues in under 10 minutes that manual audits take hours to discover
Covers jailbreaks, prompt injection, tool hijacking, instruction following failures

competitors.title: ZioSec — Continuous AI Agent Penetration Testing Platform
key_points: Autonomous adversarial testing with continuous deep-chained attacks against AI agents
Findings mapped to OWASP AISVS, MITRE ATLAS, ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act
Produces audit-ready evidence for compliance frameworks
Enterprise-focused: any agent, any framework
Based in Boulder, CO — founded 2024

competitors.title: BreakMyAgent — Open-Source Red-Teaming Sandbox for LLM System Prompts
key_points: Open-source sandbox that runs automated barrage of 12 baseline attack vectors concurrently
Uses LLM-as-a-Judge with GPT-4.1-mini for systematic evaluation
Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, and open-weight models via OpenRouter
Streamlit UI + FastAPI backend, managed with uv
Tests: Direct leaks, XSS payloads, Context overflows, and more
Focused on system prompt security testing

stats.fact: DeepTeam (open-source LLM red teaming framework) has 2,180+ GitHub stars and supports 50+ vulnerability types across 7 categories
G0 scans 1,200+ risk patterns across 12 domains with 4,000+ adversarial payloads for AI agent security
Nyx finds AI agent failure modes in under 10 minutes that manual audits take hours to discover
OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 is the industry standard for LLM vulnerability classification
OWASP Top 10 for Agents 2026 specifically addresses agentic AI security vulnerabilities including goal theft, recursive hijacking, and excessive agency
ZioSec maps findings to OWASP AISVS, MITRE ATLAS, ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF, and EU AI Act for compliance readiness
G0 detects 19 AI developer tools including Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, Zed, JetBrains, Gemini CLI, and more for endpoint assessment

angles: The shift from manual to automated red teaming is essential as AI agents gain tool access and autonomy — traditional penetration testing methodologies don't apply to natural language attack surfaces
Multi-turn adaptive attacks (crescendo jailbreaking, tree jailbreaking) represent the cutting edge of AI agent red teaming, going far beyond single-shot prompt injection
Compliance frameworks are converging: OWASP, NIST AI RMF, MITRE ATLAS, ISO 42001, and EU AI Act all now have AI-specific security requirements that automated red teaming can address
The MCP (Model Context Protocol) supply chain is a rapidly growing attack surface — tools like G0 now scan for MCP server vulnerabilities, rug-pulls, and hardcoded secrets
Open-source tools (DeepTeam, BreakMyAgent, G0) are democratizing AI red teaming, making it accessible to startups and individual developers, not just enterprise security teams
LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation is becoming the standard approach for automated red teaming assessment, replacing manual human review
